parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent of Node 1: V-001 receives crude feed and separates gas, oil and free water by density at nominal 60 psig and 130 °F. Water goes to water treatment, gas to fuel gas (excess to the burn pit) and oil to the Heater–Treater ahead of the V-003 desalter. The source elements (Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop) were combined with the No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion and Error guidewords. These were applied across the inlet, gas, oil, water and relief boundaries. The highest priorities are: V-001 overpressure (F01); low level with gas blow-by to the Heater–Treater (F07); fire/explosion from loss of containment (F15); liquid carryover to fuel gas and the burn pit (F06); and corrosion/erosion with no identified safeguard (F12). The only source-supported procedural item, start-up without bypass opening, is F13. The Medium-ranked items have mainly operational or downstream consequences, or unresolved credibility. These cover inlet flow, low pressure, interface, temperature, reverse flow and shutdown. Safeguard credit is provisional because several data are not supplied: instrument services, trip logic, level and temperature instrumentation, relief destination, E-001 duty and design limits. The 60 psig versus 125 psig/200 °F discrepancy must be reconciled before PSV adequacy can be concluded.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Organizational factors (management systems, staffing, safety culture): not assessed. There is no packet evidence, and the source cautions against inventing organizational facts (SYS-09).
Pump-related deviations (cavitation, deadheading, seal failure): not applicable on current evidence, as no pumps are listed for Node 1 (SYS-06).
Vacuum/sub-atmospheric condition in V-001: no credible mechanism identified from the supplied data at 60 psig nominal operation; unresolved pending steam-out, draining and isolation practices.
Toxic (H2S) release consequences: unresolved, as fluid composition is not supplied.
Sand/solids erosion and accumulation: unresolved, as the presence of solids is not confirmed (F12, F17).
Wax/hydrate formation at low temperature: unresolved, as crude/gas properties and ambient conditions are not supplied (F11).
Reverse-flow credibility and severity: unresolved pending the pressure profile and non-return valve data (F05).
E-001 internal leak and temperature-control consequences: unresolved, as the exchanger duty, medium and location are not specified (F10–F12).
Downstream nodes (Heater–Treater, V-003 desalter, water treatment, fuel gas users, burn pit): outside Node 1. Interface consequences are noted but not analysed.
Human decision errors beyond the start-up bypass item are not source-supported. Generic line-up and alarm-response causes are included only as unverified possibilities (F03, F07, F14, F16).
The consequence of start-up without bypass opening is not described in the source. F13 consequences are plausible but unconfirmed.

uncertainty_notes: The published Node 1 conditions are ambiguous or inconsistent. Nominal values are 60 psig and 130 °F, but the operating-condition text reads '125 psig to 200 °F', which may be design or maximum values. V-001 MAWP, design temperature and the PSV-101 A/B set pressure are not supplied, so overpressure margins cannot be confirmed.

Instrument and valve functions are inferred from tag conventions only. Line service, trip initiators, fail-safe positions and independence are not specified for PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, SDV-101, SDV-102, LV-101, LV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101 or FAL-103. All safeguard credit is therefore provisional.

Several items are not listed in the packet: level transmitters/alarms, temperature instruments, check valves, fire and gas detection, emergency depressurisation, burn-pit ignition/purge and liquid knockout. Their absence from the packet is treated as unverified, not as confirmed absence.
E-001 duty, heating/cooling medium and location relative to V-001 are not specified, so the temperature findings are conditional.
